the photo-oxiadtion of isoprene in the presence of OH radicals leads to the formation of SOA, the SOA formation is initiated through the reaction of OH with isoprene and is mainly attributed to the formation of carbonyls, which are further oxidized through OH and NO3 radical reactions to produce hydroxycarbonlys, hydroxynitrate, and other oxygenates.
isoprene photo-oxidation leads to the formation of SOA through a complicated series of reactions.

OH-initiated photooxidation of isoprne produces a variety of products, including carbonyls, alcohols, hydroperoxides, hydroxycarboxylic acids, nitrates/nitro compounds, and hydroxynitrated compounds, and some of these compounds can further undergo reactions to produce SOA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TD-VUV-PIAMS is a powerful tool in the study of SOA formation.
isoprene is a very important precursor for the formation of SOA and the chemical compositions of isoprene-derived SOA are very complex.
the TD-VUV-TOFAPIAMS is a powerful technique for the chemical identification of SOAs, especially for the compounds with low volatility, high polarity, and/or high oxygen content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoionization aerosols mass spectrometry is an ideal method for the real time measurement and chemical identification of SOAs.
TD-VUV-PIAMS can provide real-time chemical information of SOA and the PIE spectrum can be used to identify the chemical composition.
TD-VUV-TOFIAMS can provide detailed information of the SOA formation, which can be used to identify the major SOA precursors and reaction pathways.
